entry.title: Blackmagic Ambisonic Microphone: specs and price
entry.summary: 1 minute read Blackmagic Ambisonic Microphone: specs and price 2:44 Blackmagic Design’s new Ambisonic Microphone packs 108 MEMS microphones into a palm-sized 7th order array that records spatial audio over one USB-C cable. Blackmagic Design is doubling down on the immersive video
entry.content:
1 minute read
Blackmagic Ambisonic Microphone: specs and price
2:44

Blackmagic Design’s new Ambisonic Microphone packs 108 MEMS microphones into a palm-sized 7th order array that records spatial audio over one USB-C cable.

Blackmagic Design is doubling down on the immersive video product line started with the release of the URSA Cine Immersive by adding audio to the mix. The Blackmagic Ambisonic Microphone is a 7th order ambisonic microphone array with 108 digital MEMS microphones that are positioned in a sphere to capture the entire sound field in all directions.

The microphones are mounted flush in a solid, faceted metal body small enough to fit in the palm of your hand and mount on a camera.

7th order ambisonics

And in case you were wondering, ‘7th order’ describes how precisely a mic can pin down where a sound comes from. The rule of thumb is that a mic needs at least (order + 1) squared capsules: four for 1st order, nine for 2nd, and so on. At 7th order that works out to 64 channels, which is what the Blackmagic Ambisonic Microphone outputs.

As far as we can tell, this is the highest-order commercial mic available, with the only higher-order mics confined to R&D.

“This microphone started when we were collaborating with Apple on the Blackmagic URSA Cine Immersive camera. I heard a high resolution spatial audio capture for the first time and it was like hearing an acoustic reality, I was totally blown away,” says Grant Petty, Blackmagic Design CEO. “Apple licensed their array geometry and the ambisonic encoding filters, we did the engineering and design, and the result is an ambisonic microphone where you just plug in one cable and capture true spatial audio.”

One cable, built-in encoding, no breakout box

An internal processor running Apple’s encoding filters converts all 108 microphones to 7th order ambisonics in real time, so no encoding software or breakout box is needed.

Impressively, given all that complexity, the mic connects and is powered over a single USB-C cable. That helps it mount on the Blackmagic URSA Cine Immersive and record spatial audio directly into the camera’s immersive files for Apple Immersive content. It also works with a computer for recording and live mixing in Fairlight Live, and even records directly to iPhone using the Blackmagic Camera app. A USB to SMPTE-2110 converter will be available for broadcast workflows.

Pricing and availability

The microphone will be available in December 2026 for $1695 excluding local duties and taxes. Blackmagic lists it at $1909 in the US, which includes duties. The $2405 Blackmagic Ambisonic Microphone Kit adds a dedicated Microphone Mount, a windshield, and a locking USB-C cable for secure attachment.

entry.title: Adobe Firefly Build a story and video assembler
entry.summary: 2 minute read Adobe Firefly Build a story and video assembler 3:18 Two new beta workspaces in Firefly take an idea to planned scenes and shots, then on to an assembled short video. Adobe has added two beta workspaces to Firefly at MAX 2026 that between them cover the journey from
entry.content:
2 minute read
Adobe Firefly Build a story and video assembler
3:18

Two new beta workspaces in Firefly take an idea to planned scenes and shots, then on to an assembled short video.

Adobe has added two beta workspaces to Firefly at MAX 2026 that between them cover the journey from idea to short video. Build a story, found under Video in the Firefly menu, turns a prompt into a structured visual story. Assemble short video then offers a simplified, single-track workspace for arranging the clips.

Build a story: from idea to shot cards

For anyone who pootled around with prompts in the early days of AI, the rate of change is jaw-dropping. Users can now describe an idea to the Firefly AI Assistant, which asks for a target duration and optional details on characters, locations, objects, and creative direction.

It then proposes a look, a sound approach, the number of scenes and shots, and the characters, locations, and objects involved. Once the proposal is accepted, the assistant saves those characters, locations, and objects as elements to keep them consistent across shots, wires them into the relevant shots, writes a beat description for each, and generates a first frame.

Shots appear as cards grouped by scene, each showing its first frame. Frames and beat descriptions can be refined in the Shot editor or by asking the assistant, and clips can be generated card by card or for every card at once with Generate all. The finished sequence can be downloaded or opened in Timeline (beta) for further editing. One catch: resolution and aspect ratio can’t be changed for any shot once frames are generated.

The Creative Agent behind the assistant also gains Plan Mode, a Model Selector, and saved preferences for formats, colors, brand guidelines, characters, and products.

Assemble short video: a single-track workspace

Assemble short video is a lightweight workspace for generated or imported clips on a single track. Users can trim, split, and rearrange clips, adjust the volume of individual clips, detect cuts, and change the aspect ratio. Selected clips can be regenerated from a text prompt, with an optional reference image, and a cost indicator shows the generative credits required before generation starts. Regenerated versions appear as takes to compare, and the sequence can be sent to Timeline (beta) for multi-track editing.

It can be reached from Video > Assemble short video, after a Quick Action workflow, or from the AI Assistant after generating with an omni model.

A year of Firefly video work

These new tools extend a year of Firefly video work. The browser-based video editor was announced in private beta at MAX 2025 and opened in public beta that December, Quick Cut added automatic first-draft assembly in February, and Adobe announced storyboard-to-video generation in June.

Availability and limits

Both tools are in beta, and Adobe’s help pages say neither is available to Creative Cloud for Teams or Enterprise users. Build a story works only in Chrome and Edge on desktop, doesn’t support viewports smaller than 1080 x 700 pixels, and takes clips only from Adobe cloud storage’s generation history, not direct uploads. That leaves Build a story limited in scope for now.

entry.title: Adobe Disney AI alliance and Google partnership
entry.summary: 1 minute read Adobe Disney AI alliance and Google partnership 2:34 Adobe is now Disney’s Official AI Innovation Partner, with custom Firefly Foundry models at the core. It has also deepened its Google partnership. Adobe has announced two partnerships at MAX 2026 with Disney and G
entry.content:
1 minute read
Adobe Disney AI alliance and Google partnership
2:34

Adobe is now Disney’s Official AI Innovation Partner, with custom Firefly Foundry models at the core. It has also deepened its Google partnership.

Adobe has announced two partnerships at MAX 2026 with Disney and Google that between them cover both ends of its AI strategy: bespoke models for a major studio, and a wider choice of off-the-shelf models for everyone else.

Disney: custom models and early access

On Monday, Adobe and The Walt Disney Company announced a multi-year strategic alliance that makes Adobe an Official AI Innovation Partner of Disney. Adobe will give Disney early access to Firefly, Firefly Foundry, Premiere, and Photoshop, along with dedicated engineering and research resources to support the Disney production pipeline.

The centerpiece of the deal is Firefly Foundry, Adobe’s service for proprietary models. Disney will work with Adobe on generative models tailored to its properties, trained on character attributes, environments, and visual styles. Walt Disney Imagineering Research & Development is already using it in the theme park pipeline, with a sketch-to-image model that turns hand-drawn concepts into rendered 2D concept art, and a custom image model that generates franchise-accurate assets.

There’s further integration across other parts of the sprawling Disney empire too, but perhaps what makes this most interesting is Disney’s track record with AI. The House of Mouse inked a high-profile deal with OpenAI that tanked when OpenAI pulled the plug on its Sora video app. It will have searched very carefully before putting its eggs into the AI basket once more, and getting Disney on board is a definite feather in Adobe’s cap.

Google: models in, tools out

Then, on Tuesday, Adobe and Google announced an expanded partnership running in both directions. Google’s latest image and video models will continue to reach Firefly, Photoshop, Express, and Premiere, with Gemini Omni, Veo, and Nano Banana already available to customers. Gemini models will also help power AI features in Acrobat.

In the other direction, Acrobat will come to Google Workspace through Drive and Gmail, Adobe’s connectors in Gemini and Gemini Enterprise will expand to include Acrobat and more creative tools, and Adobe’s creative tools will arrive in Google Search’s AI Mode. Adobe and Google DeepMind will also explore a customized Google image model for Photoshop that could allow near-real-time prompt edits with a choice of variants.

entry.content:

OWC ThunderBay 4 Thunderbolt 5: specs and price
1:25

OWC has added Thunderbolt 5 to its four-bay ThunderBay 4 RAID enclosure. Pre-orders are open from $549, with shipments due next week.

Other World Computing (OWC) has added Thunderbolt 5 to its ThunderBay 4 four-bay aluminum RAID enclosure, with capacity of up to 128 TB.

Pitched at everyone from solo photographers to busy production studios, the enclosure now has two Thunderbolt 5 ports: a host connection and a downstream port for daisy chaining additional Thunderbolt, USB4, and USB-C devices without using up a port on the computer. In RAID 0, real-world speeds reach up to 1268 MB/s with HDDs and up to 1703 MB/s with SSDs.

Pre-configured models ship set up for RAID 5, which tolerates a single drive failure. OWC SoftRAID 9 handles setup, runs continuous drive health monitoring, and supports RAID 0, 1, 4, 5, 6, 6+, 10, and JBOD. OWC + Strada, the remote collaboration platform OWC has invested in, lets a remote team browse, preview, and edit ThunderBay media without cloud uploads.

The ThunderBay 4 with Thunderbolt 5 is available for pre-order, with shipments to begin the week of November 16. Pricing starts at $549 for the DIY enclosure, while pre-configured models with up to 128 TB of capacity (96 TB in RAID 5) start from $1499.

entry.summary: 1 minute read Avid Ready to Play: AI video in Media Composer 2:17 Ready to Play adds Create Video, Modify Video, and Analyze Video to Media Composer. Avid charges nothing extra, but Gemini access needs a Google Cloud billing account. Avid has taken the wraps off Ready to Play, a
entry.content:
1 minute read
Avid Ready to Play: AI video in Media Composer
2:17

Ready to Play adds Create Video, Modify Video, and Analyze Video to Media Composer. Avid charges nothing extra, but Gemini access needs a Google Cloud billing account.

Avid has taken the wraps off Ready to Play, a new AI extension for Media Composer built with Google's Gemini models and Veo. This is the first offering to ship under Avid's expanded strategic collaboration with Google Cloud, and it adds three workflows: Create Video, Modify Video, and Analyze Video.

As with most AI tools, they do exactly what the name suggests. Create Video generates video clips from text prompts or still images, which can be extracted from clips or sequences in the project. Results go directly into a Media Composer bin. Modify Video uses text prompts to explore visual changes to existing footage, such as removing a boom mic or other objects from a shot, or creating visual variations for collaborators and VFX teams. Analyze Video uses Google AI models to generate customizable descriptions that are added to clip metadata.

Existing sequences and source material are preserved. Create Video and Modify Video generate separate outputs without changing originals, and Analyze Video adds metadata without overwriting existing metadata.

Survey data

One thing we found interesting was the survey data that Avid included with the press release announcing the new features. Avid surveyed 120 editors, in partnership with American Cinema Editors (ACE), and found that 98% of those who use AI daily or weekly agree it is most valuable when it enhances creative intent. Of these frequent users, 76% say AI has helped them work faster, and more than 80% believe AI capabilities should be built into the tools they already use.

These are impressive figures, but you will notice that they apply to editors already using AI. Arguably, folding in the responses from those who are less frequent users would make for more interesting data.

Availability and Google Cloud costs

Ready to Play is available now for Media Composer Ultimate and Enterprise users at no additional charge from Avid. However, access to supported Google Gemini models requires an eligible Google Cloud billing account, and customers manage any applicable usage charges through Google Cloud.

entry.summary: 2 minute read Adobe MAX 2026 Premiere updates: Color Mode, MCP 4:16 Premiere's Color Mode is out of beta. Adobe's MCP integrations will let third-party agents edit native project files from early 2027. Adobe has announced some fairly hefty updates across Premiere, Creative Cloud,
entry.content:
2 minute read
Adobe MAX 2026 Premiere updates: Color Mode, MCP
4:16

Premiere's Color Mode is out of beta. Adobe's MCP integrations will let third-party agents edit native project files from early 2027.

Adobe has announced some fairly hefty updates across Premiere, Creative Cloud, and Firefly at MAX 2026, including new editing features and support for third-party agents.

In Premiere, Color Mode, first announced back at NAB 2026, is now generally available. Adobe has put a lot of effort into developing this, and response from editors so far seems to have been positive. Elsewhere, there are a lot of AI assists, as you would expect from the company at the moment. The Generative Media tool brings Generate Video, Generate Sound Effects, Generate Soundscape, and Generate Music into the timeline, using Firefly and third-party models from Google, Kling, Runway, and Luma. Enhance Audio separates audio sources for independent mixing, Separate Crosstalk splits overlapping speakers into independent tracks, and Separate Sound Source breaks audio into individual elements. Generative Remove (beta) removes objects such as boom mics and logos: mask and track the object, then click Remove.

AI Assistant (beta) expands in Premiere, accelerating Adobe's move into agentic workflows. Users describe what they need, and the assistant carries out complex, multi-step tasks in the context of their work. New capabilities include applying effects across every clip in a sequence, tracking masked subjects through a frame, and adjusting color and exposure across an entire sequence at once.

As announced last week, Premiere mobile has hundreds of thousands of UMG and WMG tracks available today on iPhone, for personal, non-commercial videos. Android support for the music is coming soon, while Adobe Stock Audio remains available for commercial projects. AI Assistant is also heading to Premiere mobile, initially in private beta. Quick Cut generates an editable first cut from selected footage and a description, while Edit with AI Assistant makes edits from natural-language requests.

AI Assistant (beta) also expands in Illustrator, InDesign, After Effects, and Frame.io, as well as the Photoshop beta app. MCP integrations, in preview, allow a third-party agent from the likes of Claude and ChatGPT to call on Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, and After Effects. They run locally and work directly in native project files, with layers, vectors, bins, and sequences all staying editable.

These are coming to Creative Cloud customers in early 2027 and, if our experience of previous MAXes is anything to go by, we will hear more about them over the next few days.

New Firefly features

Firefly AI Assistant (beta) gains Plan Mode, which lets users review, edit, and approve the agent’s plan before it starts, or let it run on its own. A Model Selector picks a model for the job or leaves it on Auto-Select, and customization lets users set formats, colors, brand guidelines, and characters once and apply them across projects. Creative Agent is also now in Firefly Boards.

Always-on agents, previewed first in Firefly AI Assistant, take on recurring background work, with a dashboard in Firefly for monitoring. On a multi-week video project, for example, an agent can organize incoming footage, remove duplicate clips, and flag camera shake or audio issues for review. Again, this is a bit of a Sneak as they will be available in beta in early 2027.

Other tools rounded up

We'll probably be hearing a lot more about these as MAX continues, but for now here's a whistle-stop of the new and confirmed features:

Photoshop

  • Relight
  • Generative Restyle
  • Remove Tool (related elements)
  • Quick Compare
  • AI Assisted Editor

Photoshop beta app

  • Mockups
  • Camera Angles
  • Generative Recompose
  • Convert to Text Layers
  • Timelapse
  • Remove Ambient Effect Only

Lightroom

  • Glow
  • Blemish Removal
  • Improved Camera Tethering across Lightroom on Desktop and iPad
  • Open Eyes (public beta)

Illustrator

  • Refreshed content libraries of brushes, graphic styles, patterns, and gradients
  • On-canvas Blend controls

InDesign

  • Co-editing (public beta)
  • Flex Layout
  • Check Document and Rewrite

ASUS ProArt GR1X: US release date and MAX demos

ASUS is showing its ProArt GR1X agentic AI mini PC at Adobe MAX today. It will be available in the US on November 18.

Adobe MAX 2026 starts later today, and one of the companies making sure it has a high-profile presence at the event is ASUS.

AI is going to be front and center in Miami, and ASUS arrives with the news that its ProArt GR1X agentic AI mini PC for on-device AI in creative workflows will be available in the US on November 18, 2026.

ProArt GR1X specs and US release date

The GR1X uses the NVIDIA RTX Spark platform, pairing a 6144-core Blackwell GPU with a 20-core Grace CPU over NVLink-C2C and up to 128 GB of unified memory, which ASUS says is enough to run 120B-parameter LLMs locally with up to 1 million tokens of context. MAX demos will pair it with the ProArt Display OLED PA27UCDV, an Anti-Glare, Low Reflection (AGLR) 4K 120 Hz QD-OLED monitor with dual Thunderbolt 4 ports and up to 140 W Power Delivery, and the PA16USV, a 4K portable monitor with 12G-SDI. The company will also be showing a quad-display mobile production studio powered by the GR1X.

P16 and P14 laptops and ProArt monitors

Elsewhere, the company will be showcasing the recently released RTX Spark-powered ProArt P16 and P14 laptops, featuring up to 6144 Blackwell GPU cores, a 20-core Grace CPU, and up to 128 GB of unified memory. ASUS describes the P16 as the thinnest ProArt laptop and the P14 as the lightest. Both have ASUS Lumina Pro OLED displays, up to 4K Tandem OLED on the P16 and up to 3K on the P14, with 1600 nits HDR peak brightness, Delta E < 1, 120 Hz VRR, and an anti-reflection coating.

The laptops will be shown with the ProArt Display OLED PA279CDV and PA329CDV, 4K 120 Hz QD-OLED monitors with Delta E < 1.5. ASUS will also demonstrate local AI agents working with Adobe Premiere Pro and Photoshop through Hermes integration.

A VFX setup will use ExpertCenter Pro ET900A X9 and ExpertCenter E500A workstations with ProArt Display OLED PA32UCDMR-K, PA27USD, and PA27UCDMR. The displays are 4K HDR QD-OLED with up to 1000 nits, up to 240 Hz, 99% DCI-P3, and Delta E < 1, and support multiple HDR formats including Dolby Vision. The demo will use Blender and Unreal Engine projects. A photo editing setup will show ASUS NUC 16 Pro and QN10 machines running Adobe Photoshop Generative Fill and AI-assisted retouching, coupled with ProArt Displays.

Booth visitors can collect stamps at demo stations for giveaways, with daily raffles.

Sessions and more

There is a session to dip into as well. “Mastering Your HDR Workflow: Adobe Premiere Meets ASUS ProArt” runs today, Tuesday, November 10, 3:45 to 4:15 p.m. EST at the Creative Park Theater. It is led by Jason Druss, Principal Product Marketing Manager, Video at Adobe, and covers HDR, Color Mode in Premiere, and HDR trends.

And finally, the ASUS ProArt Creator Connect workshop and networking event takes place tonight, November 10, 2026, at Blue Lavender Cafe & Market, 1414 Collins Ave, Miami Beach, FL 33139.

entry.summary: 1 minute read Flanders Scientific VP and V Series: price, specs 2:35 Flanders Scientific's new VP and V Series bring seven new QD-OLED reference monitors from $5995, dropping XMP's onboard scopes and Look tools to cut costs. Flanders Scientific (FSI) has introduced seven QD-OLED
entry.content:
1 minute read
Flanders Scientific VP and V Series: price, specs
2:35

Flanders Scientific's new VP and V Series bring seven new QD-OLED reference monitors from $5995, dropping XMP's onboard scopes and Look tools to cut costs.

Flanders Scientific (FSI) has introduced seven QD-OLED reference monitors across two new series, the VP and V. Both begin shipping in November 2026 and mark the first new monitors since Atomos bought the company in April 2026. Everyone expected Atomos to widen FSI's offering beyond its core high-end market, and the result is the start of a new monitoring ecosystem that can extend throughout a facility.

Effectively, they are cut-down versions of the company's existing high-end XMP range. They use the same QD-OLED panels, color technology, and GaiaColor calibration and analyzer capabilities as their XMP cousins, but they exclude onboard waveform and vectorscope, Look LUT support, and Livegrade integration from the XMP C, and processed SDI outputs and the front-panel keypad from the flagship XMP itself.

FSI reasons that these functions are often handled elsewhere in the workflow. The VP Series has been designed for the post market, where accurate monitoring and SDI connectivity are essential, but scopes and look management may already be offloaded elsewhere. The V Series cuts things back even further, removing SDI connectivity as well. The result is a series of monitors that can be close to half the cost of the all-singing, all-dancing XMP equivalent.

A facility can run XMP or VP units in its primary grading suites and V Series units in complementary rooms that don't need SDI, such as VFX, editorial, or audio post.

The VP Series is available in 26.5-, 31.5-, 55-, and 65-inch sizes. Each has four 12G-SDI inputs with clean SDI outputs, plus HDMI 2.1 and DisplayPort 1.4. Quad-view monitoring supports independent color configuration for each input. The series also supports 120 Hz refresh and stereo 3D with an optional active-glasses system.

The V Series is FSI's lowest-priced QD-OLED reference monitor range, with no SDI connectivity. It is available in 26.5-, 31.5-, and 55-inch sizes with HDMI 2.1 and DisplayPort 1.4 inputs.

Both series include GaiaColor AutoCal and GaiaColor Analyzer, HDR and SDR LUM Coloring exposure tools, custom markers, and red-, green-, and blue-only viewing modes.

Pricing and availability

VP Series pricing starts at $7995, up to 30% below the equivalent XMP model. V Series pricing starts at $5995, up to 48% below the equivalent XMP model. Both ship this month and the table below shows the comparison with the XMP range.

entry.summary: 1 minute read Sirui Aurora 15mm f/1.6, 24mm f/1.4: price, specs 2:25 Sirui’s Aurora 15mm f/1.6 and 24mm f/1.4 are up for pre-order at $599 and $499. Both full-frame autofocus primes fit Sony E and L-mount, with X and Z coming next year. Sirui has opened pre-orders on two new wide
entry.content:
1 minute read
Sirui Aurora 15mm f/1.6, 24mm f/1.4: price, specs
2:25

Sirui’s Aurora 15mm f/1.6 and 24mm f/1.4 are up for pre-order at $599 and $499. Both full-frame autofocus primes fit Sony E and L-mount, with X and Z coming next year.

Sirui has opened pre-orders on two new wide-angle lenses for its Aurora full-frame autofocus series: a 15mm f/1.6 at $599 and a 24mm f/1.4 at $499, now the cheapest lens in the Aurora range. These sit alongside the existing 85mm f/1.4 and 35mm f/1.4, and take the Aurora line wider than it has gone before.

Both are available initially in Sony E and L-mount versions, with Nikon Z and Fujifilm X versions due at the start of next year.

It's been a short journey to market since pre-production samples were shown at IBC. The 15mm uses 17 elements in 12 groups, including three aspherical, three ED, and three HRI elements, and covers a 109.3° diagonal angle of view on full frame. Minimum focus is 0.3 m (0.98 ft), and unusually for an ultra-wide it takes screw-in filters via a 77mm front thread. It weighs 542 g (1.19 lb) in E-mount and 550 g (1.21 lb) in L-mount, and measures around 106 mm (4.2 in) long.

The 24mm f/1.4 is built from 14 elements in 11 groups, with three aspherical, four ED, and three HRI elements. It focuses down to 0.26 m (0.85 ft) for a maximum magnification of 0.15x, takes 62mm filters, and weighs 550 g (1.21 lb) in E-mount or 560 g (1.23 lb) in L-mount.

Autofocus, build, and video controls

Both lenses use an STM stepping motor for autofocus, and Sirui says they work with the eye detection and subject tracking of compatible cameras. Each has an 11-blade aperture, a dust-, stain-, and splash-resistant all-metal body, and a USB-C port for firmware updates.

The control set leans toward video. The aperture ring can be switched between clicked and de-clicked operation, an iris lock holds it in the A or manual position, and there is an AF/MF switch plus a customizable Fn button that defaults to AF lock. Sirui pitches both lenses at gimbal and handheld work, and claims focus breathing is low.

Pre-orders are open now with the lenses due to shop around November 16.

entry.title: Insta360 Ace Pro 3, Osmo Action 7 release date
entry.summary: 2 minute read Insta360 Ace Pro 3, Osmo Action 7 release date 2:43 Insta360's Ace Pro 3 might have FCC approval, but Simon Wyndham still expects it and DJI's Action 7 to wait until spring 2027. We've been spoiled this year. There has been a run of strong action camera releases, in
entry.content:
2 minute read
Insta360 Ace Pro 3, Osmo Action 7 release date
2:43

Insta360's Ace Pro 3 might have FCC approval, but Simon Wyndham still expects it and DJI's Action 7 to wait until spring 2027.

We've been spoiled this year. There has been a run of strong action camera releases, including a whole new platform from GoPro, the gimbal camera wars between Insta360 and DJI, and plenty more.

When the rumor mill kicked into high gear around the Insta360 Ace Pro 3 and the rumored DJI Osmo Action 7, it was easy to assume the launches were imminent.

However, Simon Wyndham thinks differently, and he presents a compelling case for why the reality might be otherwise.

In short, he argues that a busy year and Christmas discounting make a 2026 release improbable. He also says he has not been briefed on either camera, which he would expect ahead of a pre-Christmas launch. For all the stop-start release shenanigans this year, journalists and the channel were all primed to go in the background. Releasing two major cameras cold would be a brave move. His prediction isn’t even a Q1 2027 release for the new cameras, but a Q2 one.

Likely features and capabilities

On the much-rumored one-inch sensors, he reckons both companies face the close focus and hyperfocal distance problems that affected GoPro's Mission 1 Pro. He notes that DJI's Action 6 addressed this with a mechanical iris that stops down to f4, which reduces the benefit of a larger sensor. He suggests Insta360 might skip the larger sensor unless it adopts a mechanical iris, and says bigger sensors would also mean bulkier lenses, complicating wide-angle and boost lens attachments.

Could the Ace Pro 3 and Action 7 shift toward vlogging, leaving helmet and body mounting to smaller cameras such as Insta360's Go Ultra and DJI's Osmo Nano? It's possible.

Log profiles, frame rates, and batteries

Moving on to the wish list, he hopes DJI offers full D-Log rather than D-Log M, expects 10-bit I-Log from Insta360, and would like Insta360's Cine Look modes combined with I-Log. On slow motion, he reports rumors of 240 fps on the Action 7 and 120 fps on the Ace Pro 3, and expects the Ace Pro 3 to stay at 120 fps. He considers 8K60 a likely addition, and he reckons the Action 7 will keep DJI's shared battery system and the Ace Pro 3 will keep its own.

Finally, he considers dual lenses and Lidar unlikely. But given that we're already well into November and steaming towards the end of the year, it won't be too long before we know for sure
